extracted.intended_audience: young housekeepers, wives and mothers (domestic managers)
extracted.subtask_description: Practical, prescriptive guidance for running a household: hospitality, time management, prioritization, supervising servants, attention to small tasks, and preserving health and creative time for housewives and mothers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hospitality without pretension
rubrics_metrics.description: When you invite a friend to visit, do not count the cost or make apologies; welcome them warmly and give them the same treatment you give other guests ("give him just what you give John"). Do not invite people whose presence would require a great, disruptive change in daily life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain in advance if you live quietly so the guest knows what to expect; do not let a guest feel that their presence throws household machinery out of gear; avoid pretentious entertaining such as needless dances or parties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Systematize your work (METHOD)
rubrics_metrics.description: First and foremost, the housekeeper must learn to systematize her work: 'Method and management do wonders toward saving time and money.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize tasks, establish routines, and use forethought so work is efficient rather than chaotic; the distinction between hurried, never-done work and calm, productive work lies in method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dignity of domestic labor
rubrics_metrics.description: Domestic tasks are not degrading; when sweetened by purpose they are ennobling and constitute real work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not regard 'trifles' of household management as mean; recognize their moral and practical importance and take pride in doing them well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain personal cleanliness and decent appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: A wife should be 'scrupulously clean, her hair becomingly arranged, her working-gown as neat as she can keep it, and relieved before John comes in by clean collar or ruching and a smooth white apron.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even when doing one's own work, preserve neatness and personal grooming so one appears 'well set-up' despite not having servant help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical, economical dress for work
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopt serviceable clothing (dark prints, ginghams, simple makes) for daily work to preserve fine garments and economy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Save expensive trousseau pieces for occasions; be sensible about fabrics to reduce laundry and replacement costs; understand wearing 'plain attire' is often necessity, not neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Value and attention to small tasks (chink-fillers)
rubrics_metrics.description: The small, often-unnoticed chores—picking up hats, wiping smears, dusting chair rungs, mending a coat—are essential to household harmony; these workers 'fill in the chinks' of larger plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform little attentions unobtrusively; failure to do them makes the larger household efforts appear to fail. Recognize such work as an important 'mission'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supervise and give the dainty, lady-like touch
rubrics_metrics.description: While servants may do rough work, the mistress must supply the finishing, dainty touch—notice tiny defects servants miss (tiny holes, dust under table, sticky teacups).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inspect and correct small imperfections; the 'brains back of your hands' add quality that mere rough work cannot achieve.

rubrics_metrics.name: Anticipation and readiness of service details
rubrics_metrics.description: Attend to service minutiae in advance: ensure tea water is boiling, alcohol lamp is filled, flies brushed out, plates warmed, sugar and salt filled.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These small preparations prevent awkward pauses and interruptions during meals and social moments; they are like washing one's face—unnoticed if done, conspicuous if omitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Household rule: put things back immediately
rubrics_metrics.description: Resolve that each household member should put in its proper place everything observed out of order so the house remains immaculate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If everyone returned misplaced items immediately, the cumulative saving of time would free the mother for other duties or rest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect creative and uninterrupted work time
rubrics_metrics.description: Guard time set aside for writing or other concentrated work; interruptions by household duties can destroy creative projects (an anecdote: 'He was--' lost by interruptions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Set boundaries, delegate where possible, and schedule so important intellectual or creative tasks have uninterrupted blocks of time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prioritize must-haves over maybes
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Something must be crowded out.' Determine which duties are of prime importance (care of children, essential home duties) and which are secondary or expendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a 'test-stone' duty (e.g., baby's or husband's needs) to evaluate the importance of other tasks; deliberately set less important tasks aside rather than haphazardly neglecting them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Home duties precede social engagements
rubrics_metrics.description: A busy mother cannot fully serve family and society; domestic responsibilities (children, clothes, food, health) should take precedence over teas, plays, and frequent entertainments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even wealthy families should not shift primary maternal oversight entirely to hired nurses or servants; the mother's supervision remains essential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protect health and allow rest
rubrics_metrics.description: Rest and health are non-negotiable duties: 'A day in which no breathing-space has been found is a wicked day.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid constant overwork; fatigue harms the individual's character and those around her and is false economy. Reserve breathing-space daily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unnecessary talking and gossip
rubrics_metrics.description: Unnecessary conversation among servants and family wastes paid time; 'When you work, work; and when you play, play.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discourage gossip and idle chatter among staff; conserve time for essential tasks and reduce lost minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dallying and pottering—use concentration and system
rubrics_metrics.description: Two keys to time management are concentration and system: list the day's duties, choose the most important, and attack one at a time rather than flitting among tasks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not stop mid-task to straighten another; pottering leads to half-completed chores and exhausted evenings with little to show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deliberately crowd out less important tasks with forethought
rubrics_metrics.description: If something must be left undone, set it aside thoughtfully rather than huddling it amid confusion—plan what to omit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make conscious trade-offs so the most important tasks receive attention; avoid laissez-faire neglect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apply the 'cui bono' test before acting or speaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Ask 'What good will it do?' before speaking harsh words, publishing remarks, or pursuing actions that may harm; avoid bitter answers, uncharitable remarks, gossip, and needless confidences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suppress sharp retorts and wholesale criticism; remember that angry words cannot be taken back and gossip tends to return; prefer kinder speech or silence when nothing good will result.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be sparing in confidantes and scandal-mongering
rubrics_metrics.description: Making many confidantes or indulging in scandal is dangerous: those who spread unsavory tales about others will likely spread tales about you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid seeking momentary satisfaction through disclosure; prefer discretion to the ephemeral pleasure of telling woes that may be used against you.
